messages.subject: Mapping world + ggplot2
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to plot the world in ggplot2.
I've followed Hadley's instructions: http://had.co.nz/ggplot/examples/maps.html

library(maps)
library(ggplot2)
reg <- as.data.frame(map("world", plot = FALSE)[c("x", "y")])
qplot(x, y, data = reg, type = "path")

But I do get really thick lines...? Anyone know how I can fix this? Or have a better way to print a world map in ggplot2.
Thank you very much in advance,

Aurelie

messages.subject: Re: Mapping world + ggplot2

qplot(x, y, data = reg, type = "path",size=I(.5))    # or whatever 'size' you want; see ?geom_path

Thank you Ben,
Actually just tweaking the code did the trick!

p <- ggplot(reg, aes(x, y))
p + geom_path()

Best,
Aurelie

qplot(x, y, data = reg, type = "path",size=I(.5))    # or whatever 'size' you want; see ?geom_path

messages.author: d31339b95f6e694c
messages.subject: Re: Mapping world + ggplot2
parts:
On 2012-Mar-21, at 14:43 , Ben Bond-Lamberty wrote:
>
> qplot(x, y, data = reg, type = "path",size=I(.5)) # or whatever 'size' you want; see ?geom_path
No the problem comes from the syntax itself, not the size argument. The type of geom is specified with the `geom` argument, not the `type` argument. So it should be:

qplot(x, y, data = reg, geom = "path")

In the previous example you were drawing points, which looked bigger.

The last line is exactly equivalent to what you did later:

ggplot(reg, aes(x, y)) + geom_path()

Jean-Olivier Irisson
